name: Second-Order Linear Oscillator & Damping
canonicalEquation: m x'' + b x' + k x = F(t)  <=>  x'' + 2*gamma*x' + omega_0^2*x = f(t)
invariantStructure: Two energy-storage elements exchanging generalized kinetic and potential energy across an inertia-stiffness pair, with linear dissipation setting underdamped, critically damped, or overdamped regimes via damping ratio zeta = gamma / omega_0.
breaksAt: Large-amplitude mechanical oscillations (e.g. finite-angle pendulums) become nonlinear and break linear superposition and amplitude-independent period.
Active circuits or saturated magnetic cores introduce nonlinear inductance/gain that violates constant-coefficient L, R, C linearity.
Heavy-ball Momentum SGD uses discrete finite steps (causing instability when eta * lambda_max > 2(1 + beta)), stochastic mini-batch noise, and non-quadratic changing curvature.
bijectionQuestion: Map inertia, linear damping, and restoring stiffness from your mastered domain to this system—then identify one regime where the linear oscillator analogy breaks.

name: Shortest-Path Tropical Semiring Relaxation
canonicalEquation: d(v) = bigoplus_{u -> v} (d(u) bigotimes w(u, v))  [e.g. min_u (d(u) + w(u,v))]
invariantStructure: Dynamic programming over a closed semiring (S, oplus, otimes) obeying optimal substructure and distributivity, where path weights combine via otimes and alternatives aggregate via idempotent oplus.
breaksAt: Dijkstra's greedy freeze invariant fails immediately in the presence of negative edge weights because popped vertices can later be shortened.
Negative-weight cycles break Bellman-Ford and tropical semiring closure since no finite minimum path exists.
DAG topological DP fails on cyclic graphs; Viterbi requires Markov conditional independence (history beyond state s cannot alter transition costs).
bijectionQuestion: Which two semiring operators (combine and aggregate) replace (+, min) here, and what graph or edge-weight condition breaks the relaxation order?

name: Pigeonhole Quorum Intersection Invariant
invariantStructure: Pigeonhole intersection of replica subsets guarantees every new decision observes at least one honest witness from every prior committed decision, preventing split-brain divergence.

domains.title: Read/Write Asymmetric Storage Quorums (R + W > N)

variableMap.quorumSize: R + W > N (and W > N/2 for writes)

breaksAt: Crash-fault majority quorums (2f+1) completely fail under even a single Byzantine equivocating node in the intersection; BFT requires >= f+1 overlap (3f+1 total).
Dynamo R+W>N alone does NOT guarantee linearizability under concurrent writes or sloppy quorums/hinted handoff without read-repair or consensus ordering.
Dynamic cluster membership changes can create two disjoint majorities unless joint consensus or single-server reconfiguration is enforced.
bijectionQuestion: How big must each quorum be so every pair overlaps in at least one honest witness, and which fault model breaks a simple N/2 + 1 majority?

name: Boltzmann-Gibbs Exponential Distribution & Temperature Scaling
canonicalEquation: p_i = exp(z_i / tau) / sum_j exp(z_j / tau)   <=>   p_i = exp(-E_i / k_B T) / Z
invariantStructure: Maximum-entropy probability distribution under linear score/energy expectation constraints; temperature tau controls sharpness from uniform (tau -> inf) to argmax/ground-state (tau -> 0), with log-sum-exp acting as free energy.
breaksAt: Attention logits carry a plus sign (+z_i) whereas Boltzmann weights carry a minus sign (-E_i), so higher logits map to lower physical energy.
Softmax is strictly shift-invariant (z_i -> z_i + c leaves probabilities unchanged), whereas physical free energy F shifts by the reference zero of energy.
In non-equilibrium open systems or heavy-tailed Tsallis statistics, physical states do not follow exponential Boltzmann weights; in float16 ML, unshifted exp(z_i) overflows without max-subtraction.
bijectionQuestion: Map logit, temperature, and partition function Z across the two domains—and watch the sign flip: what happens in both systems as temperature approaches zero?

name: First-Order Proportional Decay & Relaxation Time Constant
canonicalEquation: dy/dt = -y / tau   =>   y(t) = y_0 * exp(-t / tau),   t_{1/2} = tau * ln(2)
invariantStructure: Rate of change is strictly proportional to current remaining quantity, creating a memoryless exponential relaxation with constant characteristic time tau and constant half-life.

domains.title: RC / RL Circuit Exponential Charging & Discharge

variableMap.rateLaw: R decays scaled by elapsed t / S

breaksAt: FSRS-6 uses a heavy-tailed power-law forgetting curve (1 + factor*t/S)^(-w20), NOT a memoryless exponential—older memories decay slower than pure exponential relaxation.
Zero-order and second-order chemical reactions have concentration-dependent half-lives and violate constant-tau proportional decay.
Nonlinear circuit elements (diodes, varactors) and small-N radioactive samples (discrete Poisson jumps) deviate from smooth deterministic exponential decay.
bijectionQuestion: What plays the role of the relaxation time constant tau here, and where does the memoryless constant-half-life assumption break?

name: Local Conservation & Flux Continuity Equation
canonicalEquation: d(rho)/dt + div(J) = 0   (steady state: sum Flux_in = sum Flux_out)
invariantStructure: Any local change in a conserved density inside a control volume equals net inward flux across its boundary—nothing is created or destroyed at interior junctions.
breaksAt: KCL fails at high frequencies where parasitic displacement current (epsilon_0 dE/dt) accumulates charge on conductors instead of zero-capacitance lumped nodes.
Fluid continuity A1 v1 = A2 v2 breaks for compressible gases when density rho varies with pressure/temperature.
Network flow conservation holds only at interior vertices (excluding source s and sink t) and adds hard edge-capacity bounds absent from linear fluid/KCL junctions.
bijectionQuestion: Identify the conserved quantity and its boundary flux here—then name one source, sink, or accumulation effect that breaks steady-state balance.

name: Spectral Decomposition & Decoupled Eigenmodes
canonicalEquation: A v_k = lambda_k v_k   =>   coupled system decouples along eigenbasis {v_k}
invariantStructure: Transforming a coupled linear operator into its invariant eigenvector basis eliminates cross-terms, reducing multi-dimensional evolution or variance to independent 1-D scalar modes governed by eigenvalues lambda_k.

variableMap.decoupledDynamics: Cov(u_i^T X, u_j^T X) = lambda_i delta_ij

domains.title: Markov Chain Stationary Distribution & Spectral Gap
Linear ODE System Stability & Phase Portraits

variableMap.decoupledDynamics: x(t) = sum c_k exp(lambda_k t) v_k

breaksAt: Non-normal or defective (non-diagonalizable) matrices lack a full eigenbasis and require Jordan blocks, causing transient amplification even when all Re(lambda_k) < 0.
Symmetric operators (coupled springs, PCA covariance) guarantee real orthogonal eigenvectors, whereas general Markov/ODE matrices can have complex or non-orthogonal eigenvectors.
Periodic or reducible Markov chains break unique stationary convergence (multiple eigenvalues with |lambda| = 1).
bijectionQuestion: What linear operator is being diagonalized, what do its eigenvectors and eigenvalues represent physically or statistically, and when does diagonalization fail?

name: Independent Sum Variance Growth & 1/sqrt(N) Normalization
canonicalEquation: Var(sum_{i=1}^N X_i) = N * sigma^2   =>   scale by 1 / sqrt(N) to keep Var = O(1)
invariantStructure: Summing N zero-mean uncorrelated terms multiplies variance linearly by N (standard deviation by sqrt(N)), so dividing by sqrt(N) is the unique scale preserving unit variance and preventing saturation or blow-up.

domains.title: Xavier / Glorot & He Kaiming Weight Initialization
Central Limit Theorem & Standard Error (sigma / sqrt(n))

breaksAt: If summands are positively correlated (Cov(X_i, X_j) > 0), variance grows as O(N^2) rather than O(N), so 1/sqrt(N) under-normalizes (e.g. aligned Q/K features or deep residual branches).
ReLU zeroes half the distribution, halving variance per layer—so Xavier 1/sqrt(n_in) shrinks activations exponentially and must be adjusted to He sqrt(2/n_in).
Heavy-tailed distributions with infinite variance (e.g. Cauchy) violate the Central Limit Theorem and never stabilize under 1/sqrt(n) scaling.
bijectionQuestion: What N uncorrelated terms are being summed here so variance grows by N, and what happens when independence or zero-mean assumptions break?

name: Variational Equilibrium & Second-Order Curvature Stability
invariantStructure: Spontaneous dynamics move down the gradient of a scalar potential; equilibrium occurs where first derivative vanishes, and stability against perturbations requires strictly positive second-derivative curvature.

domains.title: Gibbs Free Energy Minimization & Chemical Equilibrium

breaksAt: First-order stationarity alone cannot distinguish a stable minimum from an unstable maximum or saddle point—second-order curvature (or higher derivatives when curvature is zero) is mandatory.
Gibbs free energy minimization only governs constant-T, constant-P closed systems; isolated systems maximize entropy S instead, and kinetic barriers can trap metastable states.
Non-convex neural loss landscapes and non-conservative forces (curl F != 0) have no global scalar minimum guarantee; discrete gradient descent can overshoot even at a strict minimum.
bijectionQuestion: Identify the scalar potential, its zero-gradient equilibrium condition, and the positive curvature condition—then name one case where zero gradient is NOT a stable minimum.

name: Constrained Optimization Duality & Conjugate Multipliers
canonicalEquation: L(x, lambda) = f(x) + lambda^T g(x)   =>   grad_x f = -lambda^T grad_x g
invariantStructure: Converting hard constraints or state variables into conjugate dual prices/forces (multipliers or Legendre slopes) turns constrained primal optima into unconstrained saddle points whose dual variables quantify exact marginal sensitivity.

domains.title: SVM Dual Problem & KKT Complementary Slackness

variableMap.saddleFunction: L(w, b, alpha) = (1/2)||w||^2 - sum alpha_i margin_i

variableMap.primalProblem: internal energy U(S, V) over extensive vars
variableMap.saddleFunction: F = U - T S,  G = U - T S + P V

Equality Lagrange multipliers can have either sign, whereas inequality constraints (SVM/KKT) strictly require dual feasibility alpha_i >= 0 and complementary slackness.
Legendre transforms lose information across non-convex phase-transition regions (where the double transform returns only the convex hull, requiring Maxwell construction).
bijectionQuestion: What plays the role of the dual multiplier or conjugate slope here, what sensitivity does it measure, and what non-convexity breaks strong duality?
